parole.testo: The same word as Greek μακάρι (makári), Romanian măcar, Italian magari, Spanish maguer, Andalusian Arabic مكار (ma(k)kār, “even, at least”). Probably from Ancient Greek μακάριος (makários), perhaps through the interjection ὦ μακάριε (ô makárie, “lucky you!”). While this etymology is generally accept

parole.significato: brood of vipers; generation of vipers; address used by Jesus for the Pharisees and Sadducees (three times in Matthew),…
parole.testo: From nisel + lifgħat. Calque of Ancient Greek γεννήματα ἐχιδνῶν (gennḗmata ekhidnôn).

Eventually from Latin fascia. Regarding the preserved velar/uvular, the form cannot have passed through Sicilian fascia, whence indeed Maltese faxxa.
